0_36.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
0_36.message: This is a calm window for bonding. Small, simple interactions help your child feel safe and connected.
steps: Sit on the floor with {childName}.
Hold one soft toy and let {childName} touch it.
Say one calm word slowly and smile.

36_72.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
36_72.message: Calm moments are ideal for meaningful talk. A short story activity can strengthen communication.
steps: Pick one short picture story.
Ask {childName} what they see on each page.
End with one warm sentence: "I loved this time with you."

72_plus.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
72_plus.message: Calm periods support emotional learning. A short reflection builds confidence and trust.
steps: Sit together in a quiet spot.
Ask one question: "What felt good today?"
Share one proud moment from your side too.

0_36.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
0_36.message: High energy is easier to guide than to suppress. Channeling it now helps transition smoother later.
steps: Start one active game (jumping, claps, or quick run).
Set a short timer and do the activity together.
Slow down with deep breaths for 30 seconds.

36_72.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
36_72.message: Use this energy window for structured play before winding down later.
steps: Pick one movement game (obstacle course or dance).
Play together for 5-8 minutes.
End with a calm transition cue.

72_plus.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
72_plus.message: Channel energy into a short challenge to support focus and regulation.
steps: Set a 5-minute movement challenge.
Cheer effort, not outcome.
Cool down with water and a quiet minute.

0_36.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
0_36.message: When your child is fussy, regulation comes before instruction. First comfort, then reconnect.
steps: Move to a low-noise corner.
Offer a hug or sit close quietly.
Use a soft phrase: "I am here with you."

36_72.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
36_72.message: Name the feeling, lower demands, and reconnect with calm presence.
steps: Get down to eye level with {childName}.
Name what you see: "You seem upset."
Offer one simple choice when calm returns.

72_plus.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
72_plus.message: A short pause can prevent escalation and rebuild trust.
steps: Step back from the task causing stress.
Breathe together for 20 seconds.
Ask: "What would help right now?"

0_36.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
0_36.message: This is a good time to reduce stimulation. Gentle rhythm now supports better rest soon.
steps: Dim lights and lower screen/sound input.
Use a quiet activity like cuddling or soft music.
Start the first bedtime cue you already use.

36_72.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
36_72.message: Lower stimulation and use predictable cues to help rest arrive.
steps: Switch to one calm activity (books or lullaby).
Keep voice soft and movements slow.
Start your usual bedtime routine step.

72_plus.subtitle: Best in the next 10-15 minutes
72_plus.message: Tired signals are a cue to simplify and protect sleep.
steps: Pause active play and screens.
Offer a snack or water if needed.
Begin wind-down routine together.

steps: Open Family Meter.
Select your child current state.
Tap Guide me now again.
